terms.definition: A recorded characteristic that can take different values across the cases in a dataset, held as one column of the file.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-003 defines a variable by the job it does in one comparison: the factor set differently, the response recorded, or a condition held alike. This lesson keeps that meaning and widens the frame to any recorded characteristic that differs across cases, whatever role it plays in an argument. A column's role and a column's level of measurement are separate properties, and the first scene names that separation for the learner.

terms.definition: The property of a column that decides which arithmetic its values will support, fixed by how the values were produced rather than by how they are stored. The four levels used here are nominal, ordinal, interval, and ratio.
A variable whose values place each case into a named group, such as blood group or disposition. Its values are labels, whether they are stored as words or as numbers.
A categorical variable whose groups carry no inherent order, so the list of groups can be rearranged without losing information. Sex, blood group, and admitting ward are examples.

A categorical variable whose groups are ranked, so the order is part of what was recorded, while the size of the step between adjacent groups is not established. A four-point adherence rating, a triage level, and a tumour stage are examples.
A variable whose values are amounts on a measurement scale, so the difference between two values is itself a quantity that can be stated.
A quantitative variable that admits only separated values, most often whole counts, so nothing lies between two neighbouring values. Nights recorded and admissions in the past year are examples.

A quantitative variable that admits any value inside a range, so how finely it is reported depends on the instrument rather than on the quantity. Fasting glucose in mg/dL and hours before sleep are examples; rounding such a value to whole units does not make it discrete.

A numerical scale on which differences between values are meaningful while the zero point is a convention, so ratios of the displayed values depend on the chosen origin. Temperature in degrees Celsius is the standard case.

alignment.note: Adopts the meaning PREM-QNT-003 already gives the term: differences are meaningful, the zero point is arbitrary, and ratios of displayed values therefore depend on the origin. This lesson adds only the consequence for summaries, that an interval scale supports a mean and a standard deviation while it does not support a ratio between two values.

terms.definition: A numerical scale with a meaningful zero standing for none of the quantity, so a ratio between two values has a stable interpretation. Fasting glucose in mg/dL, hours before sleep, and a count of nights all sit here.

alignment.note: Adopts the meaning PREM-QNT-003 already gives the term: a numerical scale whose zero is meaningful, so ratios of values can be interpreted. This lesson adds only that a ratio being arithmetically defined is a separate question from the ratio being clinically informative.

terms.definition: In this block, a part divided by the whole it belongs to, giving one number between 0 and 1 that reports a group's share. Thirty-six women among sixty participants is a proportion of 0.6, or 60 per cent.

alignment.note: PREM-QNT-003 uses proportion for an equation stating that two ratios are equal, as in a/b = c/d. Statistics uses the same word for a single part-to-whole fraction between 0 and 1. Both come from division, and the statistical sense always divides a part by the total it belongs to. The second scene names the collision where the word first appears in its new sense.

terms.definition: A number stored in place of a category label, such as 1 for female and 2 for male, or 1 to 4 for a four-point rating. The numeral is a filing convenience and carries only whatever the original categories carried.

The arithmetic mean: the sum of the values divided by how many there are. Computing it uses the distances between values, so it reports something about the cases only when those distances are fixed and knowable.

The middle position once values are placed in order. With an even number of ordinal categories, the two middle observations define a middle pair or interval unless they fall in the same category; averaging their numerical codes would assume spacing the categories do not establish. For measured amounts, the usual numerical median is the average of the two middle values when there is an even number.
The value or category that occurs most often in a set of recorded values. It needs no order and no scale, so it is available at every level of measurement.
Two sets of values matched one to one because repeated measurements came from the same case, so the file could be written with one row per pair.
Two sets of values from separate cases, with no case appearing in both and no value in one set tied to a particular value in the other.
